roadmapTask: Horizon 13 of the agent-agnostic-browser-bridge project (roadmap rev2 after a second REPLAN): add viewport-default and single-element (CDP clip rect, element addressed by a findElement CSS-locator ref) screenshots to the standalone tools/chrome-bridge tool, extending the existing captureTab action in place across the parity surface with a flat too-large result-size guard, closed by a mandatory live-Chrome head-to-head verification. Full-page (captureBeyondViewport) capture was dropped in rev1 after a phase-0 probe proved it non-functional on the deliberately-unfocused sandbox tab. Rev2: the rev1 verification attempt found the shipped size-guard ceiling (600_000) sits below the real ~845KB viewport base64 and so breaks the default viewport capture, that server.ts never surfaces the width/height metadata the cross-check needs, and that an un-scrolled below-the-fold element captures blank on the unfocused tab (h10 render-pass suspension) - so a corrective phase is added and the verification phase is narrowed to an element scrolled into view first, with un-scrolled below-the-fold capture deferred behind the same render-the-tab prerequisite full-page sits behind.

dimensionScores.evidence: All coupled surface members carry the new fields in one change-set: types.ts CaptureTabParams mode/elementRef + discriminated CaptureTabResult (captured/width/height/clipped and reason/size/limit) + PageActionParams/PageActionResults entries; tool-catalog.ts captureTab schema (optional mode enum + optional elementRef, no required); tool-catalog.unit.test.ts asserts the schema and the retained len-20 assertion passes. A 10 vs a 9: grep captureBeyondViewport src/ is empty AND git diff --quiet extension/manifest.json is empty — the probe-only field is fully gone and no permission was added — plus README documents both modes and the too-large outcome. npm run verify green (tsc/eslint/338 tests; PAGE_ACTIONS still 20).

page-actions.ts resolves the ref via Runtime.evaluate document.querySelector(ref).getBoundingClientRect() (no new CDP DOM.getBoxModel dependency). The three misses are distinct named non-throws: element-not-found, zero-area gated on width<=0||height<=0 (no degenerate CDP clip call), and tab-unavailable with detail. A 10 vs a 9: the outcomes are discriminated by a `reason` field rather than one generic error string, and the tab-unavailable path is covered by three distinct tests (debugger-reject, evaluate-reject, resolver-reject), not just one.

page-actions.ts exports MAX_SCREENSHOT_BASE64_CHARS=600_000 as a documented sibling of MAX_EXECUTE_SCRIPT_RESULT_CHARS (same file, adjacent); captureImageOutcome strips the data: prefix and compares payload.length, returning { captured:false, reason:'too-large', size, limit } with no downscale/re-capture; the guard runs in both modes because both captureViewport and captureElement call captureImageOutcome. A 10 vs a 9: both boundary tests exist (just-over AND just-under) plus an element-mode over-limit test proving the guard applies outside viewport too.

debugger-ports.unit.test.ts still pins the viewport call by deep equality to exactly { format: 'png' } via toHaveBeenCalledWith (not objectContaining), and debugger-ports.ts sends only {format:'png'} plus an optional clip; the element-mode test asserts the exact clip shape {x,y,width,height,scale} with no captureBeyondViewport key. A 10 vs a 9: the element clip shape including scale is asserted exactly, which would catch a swapped x/y or a dropped scale, and grep confirms no it.skip/it.only/relaxed matcher was introduced.

server.ts isCaptureTabImage narrows on captured:true && dataUrl:string, so the branch only reaches imageResult for a real capture and JSON-texts every non-image outcome with isError:true; server.unit.test.ts asserts the success image block, too-large text/isError, element-not-found & zero-area text/isError, and tab-unavailable text/isError. A 10 vs a 9: all four structured non-image outcomes (too-large, element-not-found, zero-area, tab-unavailable) are individually routed as isError text blocks — not just the too-large one — and the shape-guard means a captured:false result can never emit an empty image block.
